summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for recurrent abdominal pain similar to prior pancreatitis episodes, but with normal lipase levels and only mild CT findings. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and pain control, then gradually advanced to a solid diet. A UTI was treated with a 3-day course of levofloxacin. EGD and capsule endoscopy revealed chronic duodenitis, suggesting possible small bowel disease or IBD, though the etiology remained unclear. A colonoscopy was attempted but unsuccessful due to inadequate bowel prep, requiring a future repeat with full GoLytely preparation. Her orthostatic hypotension was managed with dose adjustments to fludrocortisone and betaxolol, and she was discharged home in good condition, tolerating oral intake and requiring no IV medications.
